claim: Dot1l is the only known H3K79 methyltransferase.
source: Here, we identify Dot1l (disruptor of telemetric silencing 1-like) as an interacting partner of Zc3h10 and a critical coactivator of thermogenic genes. Dot1l is the only known methyltransferase that catalyzes the sequential mono-, di- and tri-methylation of H3K79, which, unlike major epigenetic sites, is located at the globular domain of nucleosome (Min et al., 2003; van Leeuwen et al., 2002; Frederiks et al., 2008).
evidence: The manuscript cites three references (Min et al., 2003; van Leeuwen et al., 2002; Frederiks et al., 2008) to support the claim that Dot1l is the only known H3K79 methyltransferase.

claim: Dot1l catalyzes the sequential mono-, di- and tri-methylation of H3K79.
source: Dot1l is the only known methyltransferase that catalyzes the sequential mono-, di- and tri-methylation of H3K79, which, unlike major epigenetic sites, is located at the globular domain of nucleosome (Min et al., 2003; van Leeuwen et al., 2002; Frederiks et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three references (Min et al., 2003; van Leeuwen et al., 2002; Frederiks et al., 2008).

claim: H3K79 is located at the globular domain of nucleosome.
source: Dot1l is the only known methyltransferase that catalyzes the sequential mono-, di- and tri-methylation of H3K79, which, unlike major epigenetic sites, is located at the globular domain of nucleosome (Min et al., 2003; van Leeuwen et al., 2002; Frederiks et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three references (Min et al., 2003; van Leeuwen et al., 2002; Frederiks et al., 2008).

claim: Dot1l does not contain a SET domain but uniquely has an AdoMET motif.
source: Differing from other histone methyltransferases, Dot1l does not contain a SET domain but uniquely has an AdoMET motif (Feng et al., 2002; van Leeuwen et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to two references (Feng et al., 2002; van Leeuwen et al., 2002).

claim: Dot1l plays roles in telomere silencing, cell cycle regulations and is particularly well studied in mixed lineage leukemia (MLL)-related leukemogenesis.
source: Dot1l is broadly known to play roles in telomere silencing, cell cycle regulations and is particularly well studied in mixed lineage leukemia (MLL)-related leukemogenesis (Schulze et al., 2009; Okada et al., 2005; Nguyen and Zhang, 2011; Ng et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to four references (Schulze et al., 2009; Okada et al., 2005; Nguyen and Zhang, 2011; Ng et al., 2002).

claim: Dot1l directly interacts with Zc3h10.
source: Indeed, we detected FLAG-Zc3h10 upon immunoprecipitation with HA antibodies. Conversely, HA-Dot1l was detected upon immunoprecipitation with FLAG antibodies (Figure 1A, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by Co-IP experimental data shown in Figure 1A, demonstrating interaction between tagged Dot1l and Zc3h10 proteins.

claim: Endogenous Dot1l and Zc3h10 interact in BAT from mice.
source: We then tested an interaction of the two endogenous proteins using BAT from mice. Again, we detected the presence of endogenous Zc3h10 when nuclear extracts of BAT from mice were immunoprecipitated with Dot1l antibody. By reverse Co-IP, we confirmed the interaction between endogenous Dot1l and Zc3h10 (Figure 1A, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by Co-IP experimental data using endogenous proteins from BAT tissue shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Cold exposure does not modulate the Zc3h10-Dot1l interaction.
source: However, the interaction of Dot1l and Zc3h10 did not change between conditions, and cold exposure does not modulate the Zc3h10-Dot1l interaction (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B comparing BAT lysates from mice at room temperature or 4°C.

claim: Dot1l can directly bind Zc3h10.
source: Incubation of GST-Dot1l fusion protein immobilized on glutathione beads with in vitro transcribed and translated [35S]-Zc3h10, but not control GST-alone, detected the presence of Zc3h10 (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 1B demonstrating direct binding between purified GST-Dot1l and in vitro translated Zc3h10.

claim: The middle fragment (501–1000) of Dot1l, that contains coiled coil motifs, interacts with Zc3h10.
source: By Co-IP, we detected the middle fragment (501–1000) of Dot1l, that contains coiled coil motifs, interacting with Zc3h10, but not the other two regions of Dot1l (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Co-IP experimental data using truncated Dot1l constructs shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Dot1l was enriched in mouse BAT compared to other tissues tested, such as WAT, liver, and kidney.
source: Indeed, tissue expression profiling by RT-qPCR and immunoblotting showed that Dot1l was enriched in mouse BAT compared to other tissues tested, such as WAT, liver, and kidney (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1D comparing Dot1l expression across different tissues.

claim: Dot1l is enriched in the brown adipocyte fraction by over 2-fold compared to the SVF.
source: We found Dot1l to be enriched in the brown adipocyte fraction by over 2-fold compared to the SVF (Figure 1E, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1E comparing Dot1l expression between adipocyte fraction and SVF.

claim: Expression of Dot1l in BAT was induced upon cold exposure.
source: Moreover, similar to Zc3h10, expression of Dot1l in BAT was induced upon cold exposure (Figure 1E, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1E comparing Dot1l expression in BAT from mice housed at 30°C or 4°C.

claim: Dot1l mRNA level was increased during BAT cell differentiation.
source: More importantly, similar to Zc3h10, Dot1l mRNA level was increased during BAT cell differentiation (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1F measuring Dot1l expression during the course of BAT cell differentiation.

claim: Zc3h10 alone activated the Ucp1 promoter over 3-fold.
source: As expected, compared to empty vector control, Zc3h10 alone activated the Ucp1 promoter over 3-fold.
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data comparing Zc3h10 transfection to empty vector control.

claim: Dot1l alone could not activate the Ucp1 promoter.
source: Dot1l alone could not activate the Ucp1 promoter.
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data testing Dot1l alone.

claim: When co-transfected with Zc3h10, Dot1l was able to synergistically activate the Ucp1 promoter, resulting in a robust 11-fold increase in the Ucp1 promoter activity.
source: When co-transfected with Zc3h10, Dot1l was able to synergistically activate the Ucp1 promoter, resulting in a robust 11-fold increase in the Ucp1 promoter activity (Figure 1G, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 1G comparing co-transfection of Zc3h10 and Dot1l to individual transfections.

claim: Cotransfection of Dot1l-M55L along with Zc3h10 and the Ucp1-luc significantly reduced the increase in the Ucp1 promoter activity compared to WT-Dot1l with Zc3h10.
source: However, cotransfection of Dot1l-M55L along with Zc3h10 and the Ucp1-luc significantly reduced the increase in the Ucp1 promoter activity compared to WT-Dot1l with Zc3h10 (Figure 1G, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 1G comparing WT-Dot1l and M55L-Dot1l mutant.

claim: EPZ5676 treatment significantly decreased the Ucp1 promoter activation by Dot1l and Zc3h10.
source: Furthermore, we also treated HEK293 cells cotransfected with WT-Dot1l and Zc3h10 with EPZ5676, a specific inhibitor of Dot1l H3K79 methyltransferase known to bind at the S-adenosyl methionine (SAM) binding pocket (Daigle et al., 2013). We detected significantly decrease in the Ucp1 promoter activation by Dot1l and Zc3h10 (Figure 1G, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 1G using EPZ5676 inhibitor treatment, with citation to Daigle et al., 2013 for the inhibitor mechanism.

claim: Both Zc3h10 and Dot1l showed strong enrichment at the - 4.6 kb region of the Ucp1 promoter.
source: By using Flag (for Zc3h10) and HA (for Dot1l) antibodies, we detected strong enrichment of both Zc3h10 and Dot1l at the - 4.6 kb region of the Ucp1 promoter, a region corresponding to the Zc3h10-binding site (Yi et al., 2019; Figure 1H, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1H, with citation to Yi et al., 2019 for the Zc3h10-binding site.

claim: Dot1l and Zc3h10 co-occupy the same regions of Tfam and Ucp1 promoters.
source: Indeed, we observed significant enrichment of Dot1l for the −4.6 kb region of the Ucp1 promoter as well as +50 bp Tfam promoter region, similar to Zc3h10 enrichment alone. However, there was no enrichment observed in the control, Gapdh promoter (Figure 1H, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by Re-ChIP experimental data shown in Figure 1H demonstrating co-occupancy of Dot1l and Zc3h10.

claim: Transduction of shDot1l adenovirus in BAT cells caused a decrease in Dot1l mRNA levels by approximately 60%.
source: Transduction of shDot1l adenovirus in BAT cells caused a decrease in Dot1l mRNA levels by approximately 60% (Figure 2A, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2A measuring Dot1l knockdown efficiency.

claim: Dot1l knockdown resulted in a 50% reduction in Ucp1 expression at mRNA and protein levels.
source: While there were no apparent changes in expression of transcription factors critical for brown adipocyte differentiation, such as Pparg, there was a 50% reduction in Ucp1 expression at mRNA and protein levels (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2A comparing control and Dot1l KD BAT cells.

claim: Expression of other Zc3h10 target genes, including Tfam, Nrf1 and Elovl3, was decreased significantly upon Dot1l knockdown.
source: Expression of other Zc3h10 target genes, including Tfam, Nrf1 and Elovl3, was also decreased significantly (Figure 2A, middle).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2A comparing control and Dot1l KD BAT cells.

claim: Dot1l KD BAT cells had decreased oxygen consumption rate (OCR) in oligomycin-, FCCP-, and rotenone/antimycin A-treated conditions.
source: Moreover, Dot1l KD BAT cells had decreased oxygen consumption rate (OCR) in oligomycin-, FCCP-, and rotenone/antimycin A-treated conditions (Figure 2B, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by Seahorse OCR measurement data shown in Figure 2B comparing control and Dot1l KD BAT cells.

claim: The uncoupled respiration of Dot1l KD cells was significantly lower than the control BAT cells in both basal and in forskolin-stimulated conditions.
source: Notably, the uncoupled respiration of Dot1l KD cells was significantly lower than the control BAT cells in both basal and in forskolin-stimulated conditions (Figure 2B, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by Seahorse OCR measurement data shown in Figure 2B comparing control and Dot1l KD BAT cells under different conditions.

claim: Dot1l knockdown had no effect on adipogenic markers or lipid accumulation.
source: Indeed, there was no difference in expression of adipogenic marks, such as Fabp4, Pparg, Adipoq and no difference in lipid accumulation detected by Oil Red O staining (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR and Oil Red O staining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A comparing control and Dot1l KD BAT cells.

claim: Dot1l inhibition resulted in a significant reduction in mRNA and protein levels for Ucp1 by 90%.
source: Dot1l inhibition resulted in a significant reduction in mRNA and protein levels for Ucp1 by 90% (Figure 2C), while not affecting Dot1l protein stability (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2C comparing DMSO control and EPZ5676-treated BAT cells.

claim: Expression of other BAT-enriched Zc3h10 target genes, such as Tfam, Nrf1, Cox7a, and Cox8b, was decreased by 40–80% upon Dot1l inhibition.
source: Expression of other BAT-enriched Zc3h10 target genes, such as Tfam, Nrf1, Cox7a, and Cox8b, was decreased by 40–80%, whereas Pparg expression was not affected (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2C comparing DMSO control and EPZ5676-treated BAT cells.

claim: EPZ5676 treated cells had significantly decreased H3K79me3 at −4.6 kb Ucp1 region as well as Tfam and Nrf1 promoter regions.
source: EPZ5676 treated cells had significantly decreased H3K79me3 at −4.6 kb Ucp1 region as well as Tfam and Nrf1 promoter regions, while having no difference at the Gapdh promoter region as compared to the control cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 2D comparing DMSO control and EPZ5676-treated BAT cells overexpressing Dot1l.

claim: Dot1l-M55L mutant significantly reduced occupancy of H3K79me3 at the promoter regions of Ucp1, Tfam and Nrf1, compared to WT-Dot1l.
source: Dot1l-M55L mutant significantly reduced occupancy of H3K79me3 at the promoter regions of Ucp1, Tfam and Nrf1, compared to WT-Dot1l, while not affecting Gapdh promoter region (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C comparing WT-Dot1l and M55L-Dot1l mutant.

claim: Dot1l overexpression significantly increased thermogenic gene expression including Ucp1, Cox8b, Cidea.
source: As expected, Dot1l overexpression significantly increased thermogenic gene expression including Ucp1, Cox8b, Cidea, while Zc3h10 KD significantly decreased these genes (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2E comparing GFP control, Dot1l OE, Zc3h10 KD, and combined conditions.

claim: Zc3h10 KD significantly decreased thermogenic gene expression.
source: As expected, Dot1l overexpression significantly increased thermogenic gene expression including Ucp1, Cox8b, Cidea, while Zc3h10 KD significantly decreased these genes (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2E comparing GFP control, Dot1l OE, Zc3h10 KD, and combined conditions.

claim: The population of ERthermAC+ cells in Dot1l OE cells was decreased by 10%, indicating increased thermogenesis.
source: Upon forskolin treatment, the population of ERthermAC+ cells in Dot1l OE cells was decreased by 10%, which indicated that the cell population with higher temperature was increased by approximately 2.5-fold (Figure 2F, Left), calculated by the percent decrease from ERthermAC+ population in control cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 2F measuring ERthermAC fluorescence in Dot1l OE cells.

claim: ERthermAC+ cells in Zc3h10 KD cells were significantly increased by 10%, indicating decreased heat production.
source: In contrast, ERthermAC+ cells in Zc3h10 KD cells were significantly increased by 10%, indicating that Zc3h10 ablation decreased heat production in BAT cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 2F measuring ERthermAC fluorescence in Zc3h10 KD cells.

claim: Zc3h10 KD in Dot1l overexpressing cells prevented Dot1l-induced thermogenesis.
source: Moreover, Zc3h10 KD in Dot1l overexpressing cells showed low ERthermAC+ cells that were similar to control cells, indicating that Zc3h10 ablation prevented Dot1l-induced thermogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 2F measuring ERthermAC fluorescence in combined Dot1l OE and Zc3h10 KD cells.

claim: Dot1l overexpression in Zc3h10 KD BAT cells had the uncoupled OCR comparable to that of Zc3h10 KD, which was significantly lower than the control cells.
source: Furthermore, when we measured OCR by using Seahorse, Dot1l overexpression in Zc3h10 KD BAT cells had the uncoupled OCR comparable to that of Zc3h10 KD, which was significantly lower than the control cells (Figure 2F, Right).
evidence: The claim is supported by Seahorse OCR measurement data shown in Figure 2F comparing different conditions.

claim: Dot1l KO pool had significantly decreased Ucp1, Dio2, Elov3, Cox8b, and Nrf1 mRNA levels by more than 50% compared to the control BAT cells.
source: We found that Dot1l KO pool had significantly decreased Ucp1, Dio2, Elov3, Cox8b, and Nrf1 mRNA levels by more than 50% compared to the control BAT cells, while Zc3h10 overexpression increased thermogenic gene expression as expected (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2G comparing control and Dot1l KO pool.

claim: Zc3h10 overexpression in Dot1l KO pool did not rescue the decreased BAT-gene expression.
source: Importantly, Zc3h10 overexpression in Dot1l KO pool did not rescue the decreased BAT- gene expression, remaining in significantly reduced thermogenic gene expression, an evidence that Dot1l is critical for Zc3h10-induced thermogenic gene program.
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2G comparing Zc3h10 OE in control versus Dot1l KO pool.

claim: Zc3h10 OE significantly reduced ERthermAC+ population compared to control.
source: Zc3h10 OE significantly reduced ERthermAC+ population in compared to control; while two independent Dot1l KO pools had increased ERthermAC+ population, indicating decreased thermogenesis (Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 2H measuring ERthermAC fluorescence.

claim: Dot1l KO pools had increased ERthermAC+ population, indicating decreased thermogenesis.
source: Zc3h10 OE significantly reduced ERthermAC+ population in compared to control; while two independent Dot1l KO pools had increased ERthermAC+ population, indicating decreased thermogenesis (Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 2H measuring ERthermAC fluorescence.

claim: Zc3h10 OE did not affect ERthermAC+ population in Dot1l KO pools.
source: Notably, Zc3h10 OE did not affect ERthermAC+ population in Dot1l KO pools.
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data comparing Zc3h10 OE effects in control versus Dot1l KO pools.

claim: Dot1l overexpression alone increased Ucp1 mRNA levels over two-fold in 3T3-L1 cells.
source: Interestingly, Dot1l overexpression alone increased Ucp1 mRNA levels over two-fold, probably due to the presence of endogenous Dot1l in 3T3-L1 cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data measuring Ucp1 expression in 3T3-L1 cells with Dot1l overexpression.

claim: Co-overexpression of both Dot1l and Zc3h10 resulted in a further increase in Ucp1 mRNA levels by three-fold and Ucp1 protein levels in 3T3-L1 cells.
source: Co-overexpression of both Dot1l and Zc3h10 resulted in a further increase in Ucp1 mRNA levels by three-fold and Ucp1 protein levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E comparing different overexpression conditions in 3T3-L1 cells.

claim: Co-overexpression of both Dot1l and Zc3h10 further increased the total OCR as well as uncoupled OCR in 3T3-L1 cells.
source: Co-overexpression of both Dot1l and Zc3h10 further increased the total OCR as well as uncoupled OCR, suggesting cooperative function of Dot1l and Zc3h10 in browning of 3T3-L1 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by Seahorse OCR measurement data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F comparing different overexpression conditions in 3T3-L1 cells.

claim: BAT from EPZ5676 treated mice showed significantly decreased mRNA levels for Ucp1, Nrf1, and Tfam, as well as other thermogenic genes, such as Ppargc1a and Elovl3.
source: Indeed, BAT from the inhibitor treated mice showed significantly decreased mRNA levels for Ucp1, Nrf1, and Tfam, as well as other thermogenic genes, such as Ppargc1a and Elovl3, while no changes in adipogenic transcription factor, such as Pparg (Figure 3B, middle).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3B comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice.

claim: Immunoblotting detected significantly lower Ucp1 protein levels in BAT of EPZ5676 treated mice compared to the control mice.
source: Also, the immunoblotting detected significantly lower Ucp1 protein levels in BAT of EPZ5676 treated mice compared to the control mice (Figure 3B, middle).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3B comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice.

claim: EPZ5676 treatment decreased thermogenic gene expression in iWAT.
source: Similarly, EPZ5676 treatment also decreased thermogenic gene expression in iWAT, WAT depot known to undergo browning (Figure 3B, right), but not in pWAT or in liver (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3B comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice in iWAT.

claim: EPZ5676 treatment did not affect thermogenic gene expression in pWAT or in liver.
source: Similarly, EPZ5676 treatment also decreased thermogenic gene expression in iWAT, WAT depot known to undergo browning (Figure 3B, right), but not in pWAT or in liver (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice in pWAT and liver.

claim: After 4 hr of cold exposure, the body temperature of the EPZ5676-treated mice was 4°C lower compared to their non-treated littermates.
source: After 4 hr of cold exposure, the body temperature of the EPZ5676-treated mice was 4°C lower compared to their non-treated littermates, demonstrating the significantly reduced thermogenic capacity (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by rectal temperature measurement data shown in Figure 3C comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice during cold exposure.

claim: EPZ5676 treated mice had significantly lower VO2 than the control mice at 4°C.
source: Indeed, EPZ5676 treated mice had significantly lower VO2 than the control mice at 4°C (Figure 3D), whereas food intake and locomotive activity were similar between the two groups (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by indirect calorimetry data shown in Figure 3D comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice.

claim: Food intake and locomotive activity were similar between control and EPZ5676-treated mice.
source: Indeed, EPZ5676 treated mice had significantly lower VO2 than the control mice at 4°C (Figure 3D), whereas food intake and locomotive activity were similar between the two groups (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by food intake and locomotor activity measurement data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice.

claim: Dot1l-BKO mice had a 70% reduction in Dot1l mRNA and protein levels in BAT.
source: Dot1l-BKO mice had a 70% reduction in Dot1l mRNA and protein levels in BAT.
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR and immunoblotting data comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: Dot1l-BKO mice showed a 60% decrease in Dot1l mRNA level in iWAT.
source: Dot1l-BKO mice also showed a 60% decrease in Dot1l mRNA level in iWAT, probably due to the mild cold exposure at room temperature that can induce Ucp1+ adipocytes in iWAT (Figure 4A, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice, with speculation about the mechanism.

claim: Ucp1 expression was significantly reduced by 40% and 60% in BAT and iWAT, respectively, in Dot1l-BKO mice.
source: Importantly, Ucp1 expression was significantly reduced by 40% and 60% in BAT and iWAT, respectively (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4B comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: Ucp1 protein level was reduced significantly in BAT of Dot1l-BKO mice.
source: Ucp1 protein level also was reduced significantly, as detect in BAT (Figure 4B right).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4B comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: Expression of other BAT enriched genes, such as Dio2 and Cidea, and other Zc3h10 target genes, such as Tfam and Nrf1, were all significantly decreased in BAT and iWAT of Dot1l-BKO mice.
source: In addition, expression of other BAT enriched genes, such as Dio2 and Cidea, and other Zc3h10 target genes, such as Tfam and Nrf1, were all significantly decreased in BAT and iWAT of Dot1l-BKO mice, compared to WT littermates (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4C comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: A 50% reduction in di-methylation and a 70% reduction in tri-methylation of H3K79 at the −4.6 kb Ucp1 promoter region was detected in Dot1l-BKO mice.
source: Indeed, we detected a 50% reduction in di-methylation and a 70% reduction in tri-methylation of H3K79 at the −4.6 kb Ucp1 promoter region (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: H3K79 methylation status at the −200 bp Nrf1 promoter region and at the +50 bp Tfam region was decreased in Dot1l-BKO mice.
source: Similar to the −4.6 kb Ucp1 promoter region, H3K79 methylation status at the −200 bp Nrf1 promoter region and at the +50 bp Tfam region was also decreased (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: After 3 hr of cold exposure, the body temperature of Dot1l-BKO mice was 5°C lower than that of control mice.
source: After 3 hr of cold exposure, the body temperature of Dot1l-BKO mice was 5°C lower than that of control mice (Figure 4E), an in vivo evidence of the requirement of Dot1l for cold-induced thermogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by rectal temperature measurement data shown in Figure 4E comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice during cold exposure.

claim: The Dot1l-BKO mice had significantly reduced VO2 compared to WT littermates at room temperature and at 4°C in particular.
source: Indeed, the Dot1l-BKO mice had significantly reduced VO2 compared to WT littermates at room temperature and at 4°C in particular, while locomotor activity and food consumption were similar (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by indirect calorimetry data shown in Figure 4F comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: OCR in BAT from Dot1l-BKO mice was decreased by 20%.
source: We found OCR in BAT from Dot1l-BKO mice to be decreased by 20%. (Figure 4F, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by Seahorse OCR measurement data shown in Figure 4F comparing BAT from Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: By 13 weeks, the Dot1l-BKO mice were approximately 8 g heavier relative to the control mice.
source: By 13 weeks, the Dot1l-BKO mice were approximately 8 g heavier relative to the control mice (Figure 4G), and the Dot1l-BKO had significantly larger iWAT and pWAT depots, which primarily accounted for the higher total body weights of Dot1l-BKO mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by body weight measurement data shown in Figure 4G comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice on HFD.

claim: The Dot1l-BKO had significantly larger iWAT and pWAT depots, which primarily accounted for the higher total body weights of Dot1l-BKO mice.
source: By 13 weeks, the Dot1l-BKO mice were approximately 8 g heavier relative to the control mice (Figure 4G), and the Dot1l-BKO had significantly larger iWAT and pWAT depots, which primarily accounted for the higher total body weights of Dot1l-BKO mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by tissue mass measurement data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: Blood glucose levels of Dot1l-BKO mice on HFD were significantly higher during the course of glucose tolerance test (GTT).
source: In addition, blood glucose levels of Dot1l-BKO mice on HFD were significantly higher during the course of glucose tolerance test (GTT) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Left), and they had significantly impaired insulin sensitivity when subjected to an insulin tolerance test (ITT) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Right).
evidence: The claim is supported by GTT data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice on HFD.

claim: Dot1l-BKO mice had significantly impaired insulin sensitivity when subjected to an insulin tolerance test (ITT).
source: In addition, blood glucose levels of Dot1l-BKO mice on HFD were significantly higher during the course of glucose tolerance test (GTT) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Left), and they had significantly impaired insulin sensitivity when subjected to an insulin tolerance test (ITT) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Right).
evidence: The claim is supported by ITT data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice on HFD.

claim: Zc3h10 overexpressing mice by injection had increased expression of BAT-enriched genes, such as Ucp1, Cox8b, and Cidea, compared to the control mice.
source: As we previously have reported that overexpression of Zc3h10 in adipose tissue enhances thermogenic gene expression (Yi et al., 2019), Zc3h10 overexpressing mice by injection had increased expression of BAT-enriched genes, such as Ucp1, Cox8b, and Cidea, compared to the control mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data comparing GFP control and Zc3h10 OE mice, with citation to Yi et al., 2019 for previous findings.

claim: Expression of BAT-enriched genes remained significantly reduced in Dot1l-BKO even upon Zc3h10 overexpression.
source: More importantly, expression BAT-enriched genes remained significantly reduced in Dot1l-BKO even upon Zc3h10 overexpression, while adipogenic markers, such as Pparg, remained unchanged (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4H comparing WT+GFP, WT+Zc3h10 OE, and Dot1l-BKO+Zc3h10 OE mice.

claim: Zc3h10 OE mice had higher core body temperature compared to the control mice after 4 hr of cold exposure.
source: Moreover, when these mice were subjected to cold exposure, Zc3h10 OE mice had higher core body temperature compared to the control mice after 4 hr (Figure 5I).
evidence: The claim is supported by rectal temperature measurement data shown in Figure 4I (note: text says Figure 5I but this appears to be Figure 4I based on context) comparing control and Zc3h10 OE mice during cold exposure.

claim: Dot1l-BKO Zc3h10 OE mice were severely cold sensitive as their body temperature was significantly lower than the control and Zc3h10 OE mice.
source: However, Dot1l-BKO Zc3h10 OE mice were severely cold sensitive as their body temperature was significantly lower than the control and Zc3h10 OE mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by rectal temperature measurement data comparing control, Zc3h10 OE, and Dot1l-BKO Zc3h10 OE mice during cold exposure.

claim: Dot1l-BKO mice had significantly reduced peaks near the transcription start sites (TSS) in ATAC-seq analysis.
source: We detected a high number of peaks in the aggregate plot (upper) and high ATAC-seq read distributions concentrated at the TSS in the heatmap for the WT (lower), while Dot1l-BKO had significantly reduced peaks near the transcription start sites (TSS), signifying reduced open chromatin regions, as H3K79 methylation has been reported as an activation marker. (Figure 5A, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5A comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: The most affected pathways by Dot1l ablation in BAT were cell cycle, chromatin organization, mitochondrion organization, thermogenesis.
source: The most affected pathways were cell cycle, chromatin organization, mitochondrion organization, thermogenesis etc (Figure 5A, middle).
evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis of ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5A comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: Dot1l-BKO mice had much smaller peaks around promoters of Ucp1, Cox8b, and Cox7a compared to WT mice.
source: Dot1l-BKO mice had much smaller peaks around promoters of Ucp1, Cox8b, and Cox7a compared to WT mice (Figure 5A, right), consistent with significantly decreased thermogenic gene expression in the Dot1l-BKO mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by ATAC-seq peak visualization data shown in Figure 5A comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: Gene ontology of genes that were at least two-fold downregulated in Dot1l-BKO mice revealed that mitochondrion organization, oxidative phosphorylation and cold-induced thermogenesis were some of the most affected processes.
source: Gene ontology of genes that were at least two-fold downregulated in Dot1l-BKO mice revealed that mitochondrion organization, oxidative phosphorylation and cold-induced thermogenesis were some of the most affected processes (Figure 5B, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: The downregulated thermogenic genes in Dot1l-BKO mice include Ucp1, Cox8b, Elovl3, and Ppargc1a.
source: Notably, the downregulated thermogenic genes include Ucp1, Cox8b, Elovl3, and Ppargc1a as well as those related to mitochondrion organization and oxidative phosphorylation such as Nrf1, Cox20, Tomm13, and Immp21 (Figure 5B, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq heatmap data shown in Figure 5B comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: Dot1l-BKO had decreased expression of Aifm2, a recently reported BAT-specific enzyme that converts NADH to NAD to sustain robust glycolysis to fuel thermogenesis.
source: Also, we found Dot1l-BKO had decreased expression of Aifm2, a recently reported BAT-specific enzyme that converts NADH to NAD to sustain robust glycolysis to fuel thermogenesis (Nguyen et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data with citation to Nguyen et al., 2020 for the function of Aifm2.

claim: Upregulated genes in Dot1l-BKO mice involved in chromatin compaction and gene repression include Hdac3, Hdac4, and Dnmt1.
source: In fact, we detected upregulated genes involved in chromatin compaction and gene repression, such as Hdac3, Hdac4, and Dnmt1, further supporting that Dot1l increases chromatin accessibility (Figure 5B, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: About 82% of the total of downregulated genes in RNA-seq were also detected from the ATAC-seq dataset.
source: We then compared RNA-seq data to ATAC-seq obtained to identify common downregulated pathways found at lower levels using ATACs upon Dot1l ablation in Ucp1+ cells, and we found about 82% of the total of downregulated genes were also detected from the ATAC-seq dataset (Figure 5C, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 5C comparing RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets.

claim: Similar processes between RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets include regulation of cold-induced thermogenesis, mitochondrial transcription and membrane organization, oxidative phosphorylation, and lipid catabolic process.
source: Some of similar processes between the two datasets include regulation of cold-induced thermogenesis, mitochondrial transcription and membrane organization, oxidative phosphorylation, and lipid catabolic process, (Figure 5C, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis of shared genes shown in Figure 5C comparing RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets.

claim: The cluster of shared genes between RNA-seq and ATAC-seq included thermogenic genes, such as Ucp1, Ppargc1a, Cox8b, Nrf1, and Cidea.
source: Remarkably, the cluster of shared genes included thermogenic genes, such as Ucp1, Ppargc1a, Cox8b, Nrf1, and Cidea, further underscoring the importance of Dot1l in brown adipose tissue.
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of shared genes between RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets.

claim: Brown adipose tissue is a metabolically beneficial organ capable of dissipating chemical energy into heat, thereby increasing energy expenditure.
source: Brown adipose tissue is a metabolically beneficial organ capable of dissipating chemical energy into heat, thereby increasing energy expenditure.
evidence: This is a general statement about BAT function presented in the abstract.

claim: Dot1l ablation in mice using Ucp1-Cre prevents activation of Ucp1 and other target genes to reduce thermogenic capacity and energy expenditure, promoting adiposity.
source: Furthermore, we demonstrate that Dot1l ablation in mice using Ucp1-Cre prevents activation of Ucp1 and other target genes to reduce thermogenic capacity and energy expenditure, promoting adiposity.
evidence: This claim summarizes findings from multiple experiments including gene expression, cold tolerance, oxygen consumption, and body weight measurements in Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: White adipose tissue (WAT) stores excess calories.
source: Adipose tissue has a central role in controlling mammalian energy metabolism in that, while white adipose tissue (WAT) is to store excess calories, brown adipose tissue (BAT) is to dissipate energy via non-shivering thermogenesis (Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004.

claim: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) dissipates energy via non-shivering thermogenesis.
source: Adipose tissue has a central role in controlling mammalian energy metabolism in that, while white adipose tissue (WAT) is to store excess calories, brown adipose tissue (BAT) is to dissipate energy via non-shivering thermogenesis (Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004.

claim: Classic brown adipocytes contain a high density of mitochondria that contain Uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1).
source: Classic brown adipocytes contain a high density of mitochondria that contain Uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1), which uncouples respiration from ATP synthesis and generates heat instead (Farmer, 2008; Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Farmer, 2008 and Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004.

claim: Ucp1 uncouples respiration from ATP synthesis and generates heat instead.
source: Classic brown adipocytes contain a high density of mitochondria that contain Uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1), which uncouples respiration from ATP synthesis and generates heat instead (Farmer, 2008; Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Farmer, 2008 and Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004.

claim: Beige/brite adipocytes in WAT depot are recruited upon cold exposure or β3-adrenergic stimulation.
source: In addition, beige/brite adipocytes in WAT depot are recruited upon cold exposure or β3-adrenergic stimulation (Seale et al., 2008; Wang and Seale, 2016; Sanchez-Gurmaches et al., 2016; Cypess et al., 2009; Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Virtanen et al., 2009; Chondronikola et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple references (Seale et al., 2008; Wang and Seale, 2016; Sanchez-Gurmaches et al., 2016; Cypess et al., 2009; Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Virtanen et al., 2009; Chondronikola et al., 2014).

claim: Adult human brown fat or brown fat-like tissue is inversely correlated with body mass index and visceral fat.
source: Based on several cross-sectional studies, adult human brown fat or brown fat-like tissue is inversely correlated with body mass index and visceral fat (Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Hibi et al., 2016; Jimenez et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to cross-sectional studies (Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Hibi et al., 2016; Jimenez et al., 2007).

claim: A multitude of transcriptional regulators have been implicated in the transcription of Ucp1, including transcription factors, Zfp516, Irf4, and Ebf2, and transcriptional coregulators, Prdm16, Ppargc1a, and Lsd1.
source: A multitude of transcriptional regulators have been implicated in the transcription of Ucp1, including transcription factors, Zfp516, Irf4, and Ebf2, and transcriptional coregulators, Prdm16, Ppargc1a, and Lsd1 (Seale et al., 2008; Rajakumari et al., 2013; Dempersmier et al., 2015; Puigserver et al., 1998; Sambeat et al., 2016; Kong et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple references (Seale et al., 2008; Rajakumari et al., 2013; Dempersmier et al., 2015; Puigserver et al., 1998; Sambeat et al., 2016; Kong et al., 2014).

claim: Zc3h10 is a BAT-enriched and cold-induced transcription factor that activates Ucp1 and other target genes, such as Tfam and Nrf1 for mitochondrial biogenesis.
source: Recently, we identified a BAT-enriched and cold-induced transcription factor, Zc3h10 that activates Ucp1 and other target genes, such as Tfam and Nrf1 for mitochondrial biogenesis (Yi et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Yi et al., 2019.

claim: Zc3h10 activates the Ucp1 promoter by directly binding to the −4.6 kb region.
source: Zc3h10 activates the Ucp1 promoter by directly binding to the −4.6 kb region.
evidence: This claim is stated as a known fact from previous work.

claim: Upon sympathetic stimulation, Zc3h10 is phosphorylated at S126 by p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) to increase binding to the distal region of the Ucp1 promoter.
source: Upon sympathetic stimulation, Zc3h10 is phosphorylated at S126 by p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) to increase binding to this distal region of the Ucp1 promoter.
evidence: This claim is stated as a known fact from previous work.

claim: Zc3h10 ablation in mice impairs the thermogenic gene program.
source: Consequently, Zc3h10 ablation in mice impairs the thermogenic gene program, while Zc3h10 overexpression in adipose tissue enhances the thermogenic capacity and energy expenditure, protecting mice from diet-induced obesity (Yi et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Yi et al., 2019.

claim: Zc3h10 overexpression in adipose tissue enhances the thermogenic capacity and energy expenditure, protecting mice from diet-induced obesity.
source: Consequently, Zc3h10 ablation in mice impairs the thermogenic gene program, while Zc3h10 overexpression in adipose tissue enhances the thermogenic capacity and energy expenditure, protecting mice from diet-induced obesity (Yi et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Yi et al., 2019.

claim: H3K79 methylation is strongly associated with active transcription.
source: In this regard, previous studies reported that H3K79 methylation is strongly associated with active transcription (Steger et al., 2008; Wood et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Steger et al., 2008 and Wood et al., 2018.

claim: H3K79me2/3 may be active enhancer marks and may even be required for enhancer-promoter interactions to increase transcription.
source: In addition, studies reported that H3K79me2/3 may be active enhancer marks and may even be required for enhancer-promoter interactions to increase transcription (Markenscoff-Papadimitriou et al., 2014; Gilan et al., 2016; Godfrey et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Markenscoff-Papadimitriou et al., 2014; Gilan et al., 2016; and Godfrey et al., 2019.

claim: A loss of H3K79me2/3 by DOT1L inhibition led to significantly reduced enhancer-promoter interaction coupled with a decrease in transcription in MLL-related leukemia cells.
source: Godfrey et al., 2019 found H3K79me2/3 to be abundant at a subset of super-enhancers in MLL-related leukemia cells and that a loss of H3K79me2/3 by DOT1L inhibition led to significantly reduced enhancer-promoter interaction coupled with a decrease in transcription (Godfrey et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Godfrey et al., 2019.

claim: The −4.6 kb upstream region of Ucp1 is suggested to be one of so-called super enhancers (SEs).
source: We show that Dot1l is recruited by Zc3h10 to the −4.6 kb upstream region of Ucp1, a region suggested to be one of so-called super enhancers (SEs) (Whyte et al., 2013; Harms et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Whyte et al., 2013 and Harms et al., 2015.

claim: H3K79me2/3 at gene promoters highly correlates with H3K4me1/2/3 and H3K36me3, known gene activation marks in mammalian cells.
source: Steger et al. demonstrated that H3K79me2/3 at gene promoters highly correlates with H3K4me1/2/3 and H3K36me3, known gene activation marks in mammalian cells.
evidence: The claim is attributed to Steger et al. based on the context.

claim: DOT1L may inhibit the localization of SIRT1 and SUV39H1 at MLL fusion target genes correlating with elevated H3K9ac and low H3K9me2, to maintain an open chromatin state.
source: Furthermore, Chen et al. reported that DOT1L may inhibit the localization of SIRT1 and SUV39H1, a H3K9ac demethylase and a H3K9me2 methyltransferase, respectively, at MLL fusion target genes correlating with elevated H3K9ac and low H3K9me2, to maintain an open chromatin state (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2015.

claim: H3K79me2 and H3K79me3 function as activation marks for thermogenic gene program.
source: Regardless, we establish that H3K79me2 and H3K79me3, in particular, function as activation marks for thermogenic gene program.
evidence: This claim summarizes the findings from the study based on multiple experimental results including ChIP-qPCR, ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq data.

claim: The GWAS database reveals multiple SNPs of Dot1l associated with a waist-hip ratio and body mass index.
source: In this regard, the GWAS database reveals multiple SNPs of Dot1l associated with a waist-hip ratio and body mass index, further supporting a potential role of Dot1l in human obesity (GWAS Central identifier: HGVPM1111, HGVPM1114).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to GWAS database with specific identifiers (GWAS Central identifier: HGVPM1111, HGVPM1114).

claim: Dot1l is recruited to the Ucp1 promoter region via its direct interaction with Zc3h10 for Zc3h10-mediated transcriptional activation of Ucp1 and other target genes.
source: We show here that Dot1l is recruited to the Ucp1 promoter region via its direct interaction with Zc3h10 for Zc3h10-mediated transcriptional activation of Ucp1 and other target genes.
evidence: This claim summarizes findings from multiple experiments including Co-IP, GST pull-down, ChIP, and Re-ChIP assays.

claim: Dot1l methyltransferase activity is required for thermogenic gene expression in vitro and in vivo.
source: By using the specific chemical inhibitor of Dot1l-H3K79 methyltransferase activity, pinometostat (EPZ-5676), we demonstrate that Dot1l methyltransferase activity is required for thermogenic gene expression in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This claim summarizes findings from experiments using EPZ5676 inhibitor in cultured cells and in mice.

claim: Dot1l ablation in brown adipocytes impairs thermogenic gene program.
source: Moreover, Dot1l ablation in brown adipocytes impairs, while ectopic Dot1l expression enhances, thermogenic gene program and that Dot1l requires Zc3h10 for its function in thermogenesis.
evidence: This claim summarizes findings from Dot1l knockdown and knockout experiments in cultured BAT cells.

claim: Ectopic Dot1l expression enhances thermogenic gene program.
source: Moreover, Dot1l ablation in brown adipocytes impairs, while ectopic Dot1l expression enhances, thermogenic gene program and that Dot1l requires Zc3h10 for its function in thermogenesis.
evidence: This claim summarizes findings from Dot1l overexpression experiments in cultured cells.

claim: Dot1l requires Zc3h10 for its function in thermogenesis.
source: Moreover, Dot1l ablation in brown adipocytes impairs, while ectopic Dot1l expression enhances, thermogenic gene program and that Dot1l requires Zc3h10 for its function in thermogenesis.
evidence: This claim summarizes findings from experiments combining Dot1l and Zc3h10 manipulations.

claim: Dot1l ablation in Ucp1+ cells in mice impairs the thermogenic capacity and lowers oxygen consumption, leading to weight gain.
source: Dot1l ablation in Ucp1+ cells in mice impairs the thermogenic capacity and lowers oxygen consumption, leading to weight gain.
evidence: This claim summarizes findings from Dot1l-BKO mouse experiments including cold tolerance tests, oxygen consumption measurements, and body weight tracking.

claim: Zc3h10 binds to Dot1l via the 501-1000aa fragment, which is largely composed of coiled coil domains.
source: Zc3h10 binds to Dot1l via the 501-1000aa fragment, which is largely composed of coiled coil domains, evolutionarily conserved and widely known for protein-protein interactions (Mier et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by Co-IP data with truncated Dot1l constructs and citation to Mier et al., 2017 for coiled coil domain function.

claim: The coiled coil domain of Dot1l has been reported to interact with some of mixed lineage leukemia (MLL) oncogenic fusion proteins, such as AF10, to induce H3K79 methylation and constitutively activate a leukemic transcription program.
source: This same coiled coil domain has been reported to interact with some of mixed lineage leukemia (MLL) oncogenic fusion proteins, such as AF10, to induce H3K79 methylation and constitutively activate a leukemic transcription program (Song et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Song et al., 2019.

claim: Zc3h10 overexpression could not rescue the decreased thermogenic gene expression upon Dot1l ablation in mice.
source: In fact, Zc3h10 overexpression could not rescue the decreased thermogenic gene expression upon Dot1l ablation in mice, demonstrating that Dot1l is critical in Zc3h10-mediated activation of thermogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from Zc3h10 adenovirus injection into Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: Dot1l-BKO mice showed a markedly less open chromatin regions in promoter regions of thermogenic genes.
source: Our Dot1l-BKO mice showed a markedly less open chromatin regions in promoter regions of thermogenic genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by ATAC-seq data comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claim: The ATAC-seq data showed significantly reduced peaks genome-wide near the transcription start sites (TSS) in BAT of Dot1l-BKO mice, compared to control mice that had concentrated open chromatin regions at TSS upon cold exposure.
source: The ATAC-seq data showed significantly reduced peaks genome-wide near the transcription start sites (TSS) in BAT of Dot1l-BKO mice, compared to control mice that had concentrated open chromatin regions at TSS upon cold exposure.
evidence: The claim is supported by ATAC-seq data comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice after cold exposure.

claim: H3K79me2/3 is abundant at a subset of super-enhancers in MLL-related leukemia cells.
source: Godfrey et al., 2019 found H3K79me2/3 to be abundant at a subset of super-enhancers in MLL-related leukemia cells and that a loss of H3K79me2/3 by DOT1L inhibition led to significantly reduced enhancer-promoter interaction coupled with a decrease in transcription (Godfrey et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Godfrey et al., 2019.

claim: H3K79me2/3 catalyzed by Dot1l may be important in maintaining enhancer/promoter association for transcriptional activation.
source: It is possible that H3K79me2/3 catalyzed by Dot1l may be important in maintaining enhancer/promoter association for transcriptional activation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the authors' interpretation of their findings and previous literature.

claim: H3K79me2/3 mark may function by inhibiting the histone deacetylase activity.
source: These authors proposed that H3K79me2/3 mark, in part, may function by inhibiting the histone deacetylase activity (Chen et al., 2015; Kang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2015 and Kang et al., 2018.

claim: Dot1l probably works with other histone modifiers to maintain activation marks or to suppress repressive marks.
source: In line with these findings, Dot1l probably works with other histone modifiers to maintain activation marks or to suppress repressive marks.
evidence: This is an inference based on the authors' interpretation of their findings and previous literature.

claim: The decreased thermogenic gene expression in Dot1l-BKO mice is due to decreased H3K79me2/3 on promoter regions of thermogenic genes, as well as genes involved in chromatin remodeling.
source: With combined ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data, we provide molecular evidence that the decreased thermogenic gene expression is due to decreased H3K79me2/3 on promoter regions of thermogenic genes, as well as genes involved in chromatin remodeling.
evidence: This claim summarizes findings from combined ATAC-seq, RNA-seq, and ChIP-qPCR data.

claim: Dot1l ablated in Ucp1+ cells show significantly decreased expression of thermogenic genes, including Ucp1, resulting in cold intolerance with decreased oxygen consumption.
source: Consequently, our mouse line of Dot1l ablated in Ucp1+ cells show significantly decreased expression of thermogenic genes, including Ucp1, resulting in cold intolerance with decreased oxygen consumption (Figure 4C–G), leading to increased adiposity as well as insulin insensitivity.
evidence: This claim summarizes findings from multiple experiments in Dot1l-BKO mice shown in Figure 4C-G.

claim: Dot1l ablation in Ucp1+ cells leads to increased adiposity as well as insulin insensitivity.
source: Consequently, our mouse line of Dot1l ablated in Ucp1+ cells show significantly decreased expression of thermogenic genes, including Ucp1, resulting in cold intolerance with decreased oxygen consumption (Figure 4C–G), leading to increased adiposity as well as insulin insensitivity.
evidence: This claim is supported by body weight, tissue mass, GTT, and ITT data from Dot1l-BKO mice.
